Only swords can wield it. Gold is the softest, while other swords can still use the upper volume. Axes, spears and empty hands cannot cast.
item.meridian_piglin_sword.upper_scroll: Molten Sword · Upper Volume · Soft Edge
technique.meridian_piglin_sword.wind_aro: The point slips around a shield and lands on the chosen part.
technique.meridian_piglin_sword.quiver.n: A tremor sends three separate points into the target.
technique.meridian_piglin_sword.spring_b: The blade rebounds from a blocked edge and strikes forward from the other side.
volume.meridian_piglin_sword.lower.note: The forms in this scroll need a blade that bends. A quenched blade is too stiff.
codex.power.meridian_piglin_sword.lower: Once warmed through, a gold blade bends around a shield. By the time it comes free, the hilt burns the palm.
item.meridian_piglin_sword.lower_scroll: Molten Sword · Lower Volume · Flowing Gold
technique.meridian_piglin_sword.coil.not: Coil the blade around their weapon arm. The edge cuts with each tug and bites deepest as you draw it back.
effect.meridian_piglin_sword.coiled.note: A golden blade coils around your weapon arm and tightens when you try to strike.
effect.meridian_piglin_sword.coiling.not: Your blade is wound around their wrist. Keep your grip until the edge bites, then draw back.
technique.meridian_piglin_sword.molten_f: Work heat through the blade. The drooping tip can curl past a shield, and the grip burns your palm.
effect.meridian_piglin_sword.molten.note: The hot blade bends around a shield’s rim. Heat creeps through the hilt and blisters your palm.
effect.meridian_piglin_sword.quenched.no: The gold has cooled stiff. Even a flick of the wrist can no longer bend its point around a shield.
